settings.text: Written from scratch, around one idea.
The app, the web UI and the command line are all clients of one protocol, so a script, or an AI agent over MCP, can drive almost anything a person can.
The real-time audio thread never allocates, locks or blocks, and tests enforce it.
The engine runs with no window, on a software GPU with a fake clock and fake devices. That is how its tests run.
MIT or Apache-2.0; one codebase for Windows, macOS and Linux.

settings.css: body { background-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0); margin: 0px auto; overflow: hidden; }
settings.html:
<!doctype html><html><head><script>window.DAW_VIEW="bridge";window.DAW_W=348</script><meta charset="utf-8"><title>DAW screen</title>
<style>html,body{margin:0;width:640px;height:360px;overflow:hidden;background:#050709}canvas{display:block}</style></head>
<body><canvas id="c" width="640" height="360"></canvas><script>
// One of the cockpit's DAW screens, drawn only from the JTunnel live data the page is
// granted (JStream's page API, `jstream.data()`, ADR-0171 decision 10): ?view= picks
// transport, arrange, device, notes, mixer, clip, scenes, iso, isopads, bridge, bridgepads or panels (or `window.DAW_VIEW`, set by a
// script ahead of this one when the page is given to JStream inline). Everything that moves or
// blinks follows the data (the clock key's beats), never the page's own clock, so a
// render on a held clock draws the same picture every time. `?w=` (or `window.DAW_W`) sets
// the width; the desk's note grid is 600 wide.
const VIEW = window.DAW_VIEW || new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('view') || 'transport';
const cv = document.getElementById('c');
const x = cv.getContext('2d');
const W = +(window.DAW_W || new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('w')) || 640, H = 360, MONO = '"DejaVu Sans Mono",monospace', SANS = 'Inter,"DejaVu Sans",sans-serif';
const AMBER = '255,176,64', CYAN = '110,220,255', GREEN = '70,230,140', RED = '255,70,70';
cv.width = W; document.documentElement.style.width = document.body.style.width = W + 'px';
// The desk's lit pads go on a clear page, over their unlit pads (`isopads`, `bridgepads`).
if (VIEW === 'iso' || VIEW === 'bridge') document.documentElement.style.background = document.body.style.background = 'transparent';
let D = {}, dirty = true;
const lowest = {};   // isomorphic view: the lowest pitch each track has played
const history = [];  // notes view: [beat start, beat end or null, pitch, track]
const steps = {};    // clip view: steps a note started on, per clip
let lastBeats = -1;
const last = {};     // panels view: the last note each track started, [pitch, velocity]
const waves = { master: [], sel: [] }; // panels view: recent levels, newest last
const onsets = {};   // panels view: the beats each track started a note on, the last bar's

function txt(t, px, py, size, col, al = 'left', wt = 600, face = MONO) {
  x.font = `${wt} ${size}px ${face}`; x.textAlign = al; x.fillStyle = col; x.fillText(t, px, py);
}
function rgba(hex, a) {
  const n = parseInt((hex || '#888888').slice(1, 7), 16);
  return `rgba(${n >> 16},${(n >> 8) & 255},${n & 255},${a})`;
}
function frame(title, right) {
  x.fillStyle = '#050709'; x.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);
  const g = x.createRadialGradient(W / 2, H / 2, 0, W / 2, H / 2, W * .6);
  g.addColorStop(0, 'rgba(20,40,60,.35)'); g.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(0,0,0,0)'); x.fillStyle = g; x.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);
  x.fillStyle = `rgba(${AMBER},.12)`; x.fillRect(0, 0, W, 34);
  x.fillStyle = `rgba(${AMBER},.8)`; x.fillRect(0, 33, W, 2);
  txt(title, 16, 24, 16, `rgba(${AMBER},.95)`, 'left', 700);
  if (right) txt(right, W - 16, 24, 13, `rgba(${CYAN},.8)`, 'right', 500);
}
function scan() { for (let y = 0; y < H; y += 3) { x.fillStyle = 'rgba(0,0,0,.18)'; x.fillRect(0, y, W, 1); } }
function clock() { return D.clock || { beats: 0, bar: 1, beat: 1, beatPhase: 0, playing: false, tempo: 0 }; }
function blinkOn() { return Math.floor((clock().beats || 0) * 2) % 2 === 0; }
function tracks() {
  const out = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) { const t = D['track/' + i]; if (t && t.exists) out.push(t); }
  return out;
}
function section() {
  const m = (D.markers && D.markers.items) || [], b = clock().beats || 0;
  let cur = null, next = null;
  for (const it of m) { if (it.position <= b) cur = it; else if (!next) next = it; }
  return { cur, next, all: m };
}
function selected() { const g = D.grid || {}; return g.selectedTrack >= 0 ? g.selectedTrack : 0; }
// ---- the desk's pads and meter segments: raised, lit silicone ----
// A pad is a raised silicone cap: matte and dark when unlit, its top edge catching the
// light and its foot casting a short shadow; lit, its light comes up through it, brightest
// in the middle, and spills a little onto the desk around it. A pad lights at once and dims
// over FADE_MS (`?fade=` or `window.DAW_FADE_MS`, default 350) when it turns off. The fade
// is timed by the data's clock while the transport plays, so a render on a held clock draws
// the same picture every time, and by the page's own clock while it is stopped.
const FADE_MS = +(window.DAW_FADE_MS || new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('fade')) || 350;
const DESK_DARK = '#05080c', ROOT_GLOW = 0.3;
const glow = {};      // desk views: each pad's light, by key, [level 0 to 1, colour]
let deskAt = null, fading = false;  // [beats, page ms] at the last draw; a pad still dimming
function deskDt() {   // seconds since the last draw, at most 1
  const c = clock(), ms = performance.now();
  let dt = 0;
  if (deskAt) dt = c.playing && c.tempo > 0 ? ((c.beats || 0) - deskAt[0]) * 60 / c.tempo : (ms - deskAt[1]) / 1000;
  deskAt = [c.beats || 0, ms];
  return Math.min(1, Math.max(0, dt));
}
// Brings each pad's light to `want` (key -> [level, colour]): up at once, down over
// FADE_MS. Returns whether a pad is still dimming.
function fadeTo(wanted, dt) {
  const want = new Map([...wanted].map(([key, v]) => [String(key), v]));  // keys as `glow`'s
  const k = Math.exp(-dt * 3000 / FADE_MS);
  let still = false;
  for (const [key, [lv, col]] of want) { const g = glow[key]; if (!g || lv >= g[0]) glow[key] = [lv, col]; else g[1] = col; }
  for (const key of Object.keys(glow)) {
    const g = glow[key], to = want.has(key) ? want.get(key)[0] : 0;
    if (g[0] > to) { g[0] = to + (g[0] - to) * k; if (g[0] - to < 0.01) g[0] = to; else still = true; }
    if (g[0] <= 0) delete glow[key];
  }
  return still;
}
function rr(px, py, w, h, r) { x.beginPath(); x.roundRect(px, py, w, h, r); }
// An unlit pad; `s` scales its edge and shadow for small pads.
function siliconePad(px, py, w, h, r, s = 1) {
  x.fillStyle = 'rgba(0,0,0,.6)'; rr(px, py + 2.5 * s, w, h, r); x.fill();
  const g = x.createLinearGradient(0, py, 0, py + h);
  g.addColorStop(0, '#2a323d'); g.addColorStop(Math.min(.5, 5 * s / h), '#1d242d'); g.addColorStop(1, '#12171e');
  x.fillStyle = g; rr(px, py, w, h, r); x.fill();
  x.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,.08)'; x.lineWidth = 1; rr(px + .5, py + .5, w - 1, h - 1, r); x.stroke();
}
// A lit pad, `lv` 0 to 1, in `col`: opaque from ROOT_GLOW up, so it hides the unlit pad
// under it, and fading out below that.
function litPad(px, py, w, h, r, col, lv, s = 1) {
  x.save();
  x.globalAlpha = Math.min(1, lv / ROOT_GLOW);
  x.shadowColor = rgba(col, Math.min(1, .9 * lv)); x.shadowBlur = 16 * s * lv;
  x.fillStyle = '#0c1016'; rr(px, py, w, h, r); x.fill();
  x.shadowBlur = 0;
  x.fillStyle = rgba(col, Math.min(1, lv)); rr(px, py, w, h, r); x.fill();
  const cx = px + w / 2, cy = py + h * .45, g = x.createRadialGradient(cx, cy, 0, cx, cy, Math.max(w, h) * .62);
  g.addColorStop(0, `rgba(255,255,255,${.34 * s * s * lv})`); g.addColorStop(.55, `rgba(255,255,255,${.08 * s * s * lv})`); g.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(0,0,0,.22)');
  x.fillStyle = g; rr(px, py, w, h, r); x.fill();
  x.strokeStyle = `rgba(255,255,255,${.12 + .25 * lv})`; x.lineWidth = 1; rr(px + .5, py + .5, w - 1, h - 1, r); x.stroke();
  x.restore();
}
function mixHex(a, b, t) {
  const p = h => parseInt(h.slice(1, 7), 16), A = p(a), B = p(b), m = sh => Math.round(((A >> sh) & 255) * (1 - t) + ((B >> sh) & 255) * t);
  return '#' + [16, 8, 0].map(sh => m(sh).toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('');
}
// Calls `f(px, py, w, h, row, column)` for each of the desk's 8 x 8 pads, row 0 at the foot.
function isoPads(f) {
  const cols = 8, rows = 8, gap = 6, cw = (W - gap * (cols + 1)) / cols, ch = (H - gap * (rows + 1)) / rows;
  for (let r = 0; r < rows; r++) for (let c = 0; c < cols; c++) f(gap + c * (cw + gap), H - (r + 1) * (ch + gap), cw, ch, r, c);
}
// Calls `f(key, px, py, w, h, column, segment, segments, height 0 to 1)` for each of the
// meter bridge's segments: six tracks of two bars in the first 290 px, the master's two
// in the last 56, 18 segments each, segment 0 at the foot.
const BRIDGE = [];
for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) for (let sub = 0; sub < 2; sub++) BRIDGE.push({ i, sub, low: '#2fe08a', high: '#ff4a3a', x0: 8 + i * (281 / 6) + sub * ((281 / 6 - 8) / 2 + 2), w: (281 / 6 - 8) / 2 - 2 });
for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) BRIDGE.push({ master: true, i, low: '#6ee0ff', high: '#ffb040', x0: 298 + i * 25, w: 19 });
function bridgeSegs(f) {
  const n = 18, gap = 4, y0 = 8, sh = (H - 2 * y0 - gap * (n - 1)) / n;
  BRIDGE.forEach((col, ci) => {
    for (let s = 0; s < n; s++) f(ci * n + s, col.x0, H - y0 - (s + 1) * sh - s * gap, col.w, sh, col, s, n, (s + .5) / n);
  });
}
function bar(px, py, w, h, v, col) {
  x.fillStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,.06)'; x.fillRect(px, py, w, h);
  x.fillStyle = col; x.fillRect(px, py, w * Math.max(0, Math.min(1, v)), h);
}

// ---- the console panels (the `panels` view) ----
// Each panel's cell in the picture, [x, y, w, h]: keep in step with tools/live_panels.py.
const PANEL_AT = {
  launcher: [0, 0, 160, 160], status: [160, 0, 160, 80], note: [160, 80, 160, 80],
  density: [0, 160, 160, 80], levels: [160, 160, 160, 80], masterWave: [0, 240, 160, 80],
  trackWave: [160, 240, 160, 80], activity: [0, 320, 80, 40], position: [80, 320, 80, 40],
  beats: [160, 320, 80, 40], strips: [240, 320, 80, 40],
};
const AMB = 'rgb(255,150,30)', AMB_DIM = 'rgba(255,150,30,.22)';
const SEG = { 0: 'abcdef', 1: 'bc', 2: 'abged', 3: 'abgcd', 4: 'fgbc', 5: 'afgcd', 6: 'afgedc', 7: 'abc',
  8: 'abcdefg', 9: 'abcdfg', '-': 'g', ' ': '', A: 'abcefg', b: 'fgcde', C: 'adef', d: 'bcdeg',
  E: 'adefg', F: 'aefg', G: 'acdef' };
function seg(ch, px, py, w, h, col) {
  const t = Math.max(2, w / 6), m = py + h / 2, r = {
    a: [px + t, py, w - 2 * t, t], g: [px + t, m - t / 2, w - 2 * t, t], d: [px + t, py + h - t, w - 2 * t, t],
    f: [px, py + t, t, h / 2 - t], b: [px + w - t, py + t, t, h / 2 - t],
    e: [px, m, t, h / 2 - t], c: [px + w - t, m, t, h / 2 - t] };
  x.fillStyle = col;
  for (const k of SEG[ch] || '') x.fillRect(...r[k]);
}
function segs(text, px, py, cw, h, n) {  // n cells, right-aligned, unlit 8s behind
  text = String(text).slice(-n).padStart(n);
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    seg(8, px + i * cw, py, cw * .72, h, AMB_DIM);
    seg(text[i], px + i * cw, py, cw * .72, h, AMB);
  }
}
function wave(list, w, h) {
  x.fillStyle = AMB_DIM; x.fillRect(6, h - 8, w - 12, 1);
  x.strokeStyle = AMB; x.lineWidth = 2; x.beginPath();
  const n = 120, dx = (w - 12) / (n - 1), off = n - list.length;
  list.forEach((v, i) => { const px = 6 + (off + i) * dx, py = h - 8 - Math.min(1, v) * (h - 16); i ? x.lineTo(px, py) : x.moveTo(px, py); });
  x.stroke();
}
const NAMES = ['C', 'C#', 'd', 'd#', 'E', 'F', 'F#', 'G', 'G#', 'A', 'A#', 'b'];
const panel = {
  // The clip launcher, 8 tracks across and 8 scenes down: a playing clip full in its
  // track's colour, a stopped one dim, a queued one blinking on the beat.
  launcher(w, h) {
    const g = 3, cw = (w - 8 - g * 7) / 8, ch = (h - 8 - g * 7) / 8;
    for (let ti = 0; ti < 8; ti++) {
      const t = D['track/' + ti], slots = (t && t.exists && t.slots) || [];
      for (let si = 0; si < 8; si++) {
        const sl = slots[si] || {}, px = 4 + ti * (cw + g), py = 4 + si * (ch + g);
        x.fillStyle = !sl.hasContent && !sl.queued ? 'rgba(255,255,255,.05)'
          : sl.state === 'playing' ? rgba(t.color, 1)
          : sl.queued ? (blinkOn() ? rgba(t.color, .9) : rgba(t.color, .2)) : rgba(t.color, .28);
        x.fillRect(px, py, cw, ch);
      }
      if (ti === selected()) { x.fillStyle = AMB; x.fillRect(4 + ti * (cw + g), h - 3, cw, 2); }
    }
  },
  // Lines of status text: the section, the tempo and position, the selected track and its device.
  status(w, h) {
    const c = clock(), s = section(), t = D['track/' + selected()] || {}, d = D.device || {};
    const lines = [`SEC ${(s.cur && s.cur.name) || '-'}`, `NXT ${(s.next && s.next.name) || '-'}`,
      `${(c.tempo || 0).toFixed(1)} BPM ${c.playing ? 'RUN' : 'STOP'}`, `TRK ${t.name || '-'}`, `DEV ${d.name || '-'}`];
    lines.forEach((l, i) => txt(l.toUpperCase().slice(0, 17), 8, 17 + i * 14.5, 12, i % 2 ? AMB_DIM.replace('.22', '.6') : AMB, 'left', 600));
  },
  // The selected track's last note: its name and octave, and its velocity as a number and a bar.
  note(w, h) {
    const l = last[selected()];
    if (l) {
      const [p, v] = l, nm = NAMES[p % 12], oct = Math.floor(p / 12) - 2;
      segs(nm[0], 8, 10, 30, 40, 1);
      if (nm[1]) txt('#', 40, 24, 16, AMB, 'left', 700);
      segs(oct < 0 ? '-' + -oct : oct, 54, 10, 30, 40, oct < 0 ? 2 : 1);
      segs(Math.round(v), 92, 18, 22, 32, 3);
      bar(8, h - 18, w - 16, 8, v / 127, AMB);
    } else { segs('---', 8, 10, 30, 40, 3); bar(8, h - 18, w - 16, 8, 0, AMB); }
  },
  // How busy the selected track is: RATE, the notes it started over the last bar (4 beats),
  // as segments and a number; POLY, the notes it holds now, a segment each up to 8.
  density(w, h) {
    const sel = selected(), b = clock().beats || 0;
    const rate = (onsets[sel] || []).filter(t => t > b - 4).length;
    const held = (((D.notes && D.notes.tracks) || [])[sel] || []).length;
    txt('RATE', 8, 24, 11, AMB, 'left', 700); txt('POLY', 8, 60, 11, AMB, 'left', 700);
    const cells = (py, n, lit, of) => {
      const cw = (w - 46 - 44) / of;
      for (let i = 0; i < of; i++) { x.fillStyle = i < lit ? AMB : AMB_DIM; x.fillRect(46 + i * cw, py, cw - 2, 14); }
    };
    cells(12, 12, Math.ceil(Math.min(32, rate) / 32 * 12), 12);
    cells(48, 8, Math.min(8, held), 8);
    segs(Math.min(99, rate), w - 40, 10, 16, 18, 2);
    segs(Math.min(99, held), w - 40, 46, 16, 18, 2);
  },
  // Every track's level and the master's, as a bar graph.
  levels(w, h) {
    const m = (D.meters && D.meters.tracks) || [], ms = (D.meters && D.meters.master) || [0, 0];
    const vals = [...Array(8).keys()].map(i => Math.max(...(m[i] || [0, 0]))).concat([ms[0], ms[1]]);
    const bw = (w - 16) / vals.length;
    vals.forEach((v, i) => {
      const px = 8 + i * bw + (i >= 8 ? 4 : 0), t = D['track/' + i];
      x.fillStyle = AMB_DIM; x.fillRect(px, 8, bw - 4, h - 16);
      x.fillStyle = i < 8 && t && t.color ? rgba(t.color, 1) : AMB;
      x.fillRect(px, h - 8 - Math.min(1, v) * (h - 16), bw - 4, Math.min(1, v) * (h - 16));
    });
  },
  masterWave(w, h) { wave(waves.master, w, h); },
  trackWave(w, h) { wave(waves.sel, w, h); },
  // A dot a track, lit while it plays a note.
  activity(w, h) {
    const ns = (D.notes && D.notes.tracks) || [];
    for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
      x.fillStyle = (ns[i] || []).length ? AMB : AMB_DIM;
      x.beginPath(); x.arc(8 + (i % 4) * 19 + 6, 8 + Math.floor(i / 4) * 17 + 6, 6, 0, 7); x.fill();
    }
  },
  // The bar and beat.
  position(w, h) { const c = clock(); segs(`${(c.bar || 1) % 1000}`.padStart(3) + (c.beat || 1), 6, 7, 17, 26, 4); },
  // The bar's beats, one dot each, the current one lit.
  beats(w, h) {
    const c = clock(), n = 4, b = ((c.beat || 1) - 1) % n;
    for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) { x.fillStyle = i === b && c.playing ? AMB : AMB_DIM; x.beginPath(); x.arc(12 + i * 18, h / 2, 6, 0, 7); x.fill(); }
  },
  // The master's left and right levels and the selected track's, as segmented strips.
  strips(w, h) {
    const ms = (D.meters && D.meters.master) || [0, 0], mt = ((D.meters && D.meters.tracks) || [])[selected()] || [0, 0];
    [ms[0], ms[1], Math.max(...mt)].forEach((v, r) => {
      for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) { x.fillStyle = i < v * 10 ? AMB : AMB_DIM; x.fillRect(6 + i * 7, 6 + r * 10, 5, 7); }
    });
  },
};

const views = {
  transport() {
    const c = clock(), t = D.transport || {};
    frame('TRANSPORT', 'BITWIG · JTUNNEL');
    const pos = t.positionText ? t.positionText.split('.').slice(0, 3).join('.') : `${c.bar}.${c.beat}.1`;
    // The position at 92 px, smaller when it would run into the play lamp (a long song's
    // bar count, or Bitwig's four-part position at high counts).
    x.font = `700 92px ${MONO}`;
    const fit = Math.min(92, Math.floor(92 * 510 / Math.max(1, x.measureText(pos).width)));
    txt(pos, 30, 140 - (92 - fit) / 3, fit, `rgba(${CYAN},.95)`, 'left', 700);
    // play / stop
    x.fillStyle = c.playing ? `rgba(${GREEN},.95)` : `rgba(${AMBER},.5)`;
    x.beginPath();
    if (c.playing) { x.moveTo(560, 70); x.lineTo(605, 95); x.lineTo(560, 120); } else x.rect(562, 74, 42, 42);
    x.fill();
    txt(c.playing ? 'PLAY' : 'STOP', 582, 142, 13, x.fillStyle, 'center', 700);
    // beat lamps
    for (let i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
      const on = c.playing && c.beat === i + 1, k = on ? 1 - c.beatPhase * .7 : .12;
      x.fillStyle = i === 0 ? `rgba(${AMBER},${k})` : `rgba(${CYAN},${k})`;
      x.beginPath(); x.arc(52 + i * 62, 192, 18, 0, 7); x.fill();
      x.strokeStyle = `rgba(${CYAN},.4)`; x.lineWidth = 2; x.stroke();
    }
    txt((t.tempoText || `${(c.tempo || 0).toFixed(2)} BPM`).toUpperCase(), 300, 186, 26, `rgba(${AMBER},.95)`, 'left', 700);
    txt(`${(c.timeSignature || [4, 4]).join('/')}  ·  Q ${t.launchQuantization || '1'} BAR`, 300, 210, 14, `rgba(${CYAN},.7)`);
    const s = section(), secs = c.seconds || 0;
    txt(`${String(Math.floor(secs / 60)).padStart(2, '0')}:${(secs % 60).toFixed(1).padStart(4, '0')}`, 610, 210, 20, `rgba(${CYAN},.8)`, 'right');
    if (s.cur) {
      const end = s.next ? s.next.position : (s.cur.position + 12), p = ((c.beats || 0) - s.cur.position) / (end - s.cur.position);
      txt(s.cur.name.toUpperCase(), 30, 268, 30, 'rgba(255,255,255,.95)', 'left', 700, SANS);
      if (s.next) txt('NEXT  ' + s.next.name.toUpperCase(), 610, 268, 15, `rgba(${AMBER},.8)`, 'right', 600);
      bar(30, 286, 580, 10, p, `rgba(${AMBER},.85)`);
      for (let b = 0; b < (end - s.cur.position) / 4; b++) {
        x.fillStyle = 'rgba(0,0,0,.7)'; x.fillRect(30 + 580 * b * 4 / (end - s.cur.position), 286, 2, 10);
      }
    } else txt('READY', 30, 268, 30, 'rgba(255,255,255,.6)', 'left', 700, SANS);
    txt(`${(D.project && D.project.name) || ''}`.toUpperCase(), 30, 335, 13, `rgba(${CYAN},.6)`);
    txt(t.fill ? 'FILL' : '', 610, 335, 13, `rgba(${AMBER},.9)`, 'right', 700);
  },
  arrange() {
    const c = clock(), s = section(), tr = tracks();
    frame('ARRANGEMENT', `BAR ${c.bar}`);
    const total = s.all.length ? s.all[s.all.length - 1].position + 12 : 196, L = 92, R = W - 54, w = R - L;
    const X = b => L + w * b / total;
    s.all.forEach((m, i) => {

<!doctype html><html><head><script>window.DAW_VIEW="bridgepads";window.DAW_W=348</script><meta charset="utf-8"><title>DAW screen</title>

<body><canvas id="c" width="640" height="360"></canvas><script>
// One of the cockpit's DAW screens, drawn only from the JTunnel live data the page is
// granted (JStream's page API, `jstream.data()`, ADR-0171 decision 10): ?view= picks
// transport, arrange, device, notes, mixer, clip, scenes, iso, isopads, bridge, bridgepads or panels (or `window.DAW_VIEW`, set by a

const history = [];  // notes view: [beat start, beat end or null, pitch, track]

}
function rgba(hex, a) {

  clip() {

  // The desk's pads as an isomorphic note grid, as a grid instrument lays it out: a

  // The desk's unlit pads, under `iso`: the same 8 x 8 pads, every one unlit, on the
  // desk's dark. It needs no data and never changes.
  isopads() {
    x.fillStyle = DESK_DARK; x.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);

  },
  // The desk's meter bridge, beside the pads: the six tracks (left and right each) and the
  // master, in 18 segments, lit from the foot by `meters`, green to red (the master cyan

  // The console's small displays, live: one 320 x 360 picture holding every panel, each in
  // the cell the model's live-panel quads map (cockpit-3d/tools/live_panels.py, PANELS).

    for (const [name, [px, py, w, h]] of Object.entries(PANEL_AT)) {
      x.save(); x.translate(px, py);

  },
  scenes() {

settings.text: One scene, several arrangements of its items. Loading one moves everything there.
A keyframe overrides each item's place, size, crop, opacity, visibility and effects. Here the main feed steps aside.
A Move glides every item at once on one easing curve; each item can have its own delay and duration.
The show's keyframe track loads these. A sequence cue, a hotkey or a MIDI pad can too.

<!doctype html><html><head><script>window.DAW_VIEW="iso";window.DAW_W=600</script><meta charset="utf-8"><title>DAW screen</title>
<style>html,body{margin:0;width:640px;height:360px;overflow:hidden;background:#050709}canvas{display:block}</style></head>
<body><canvas id="c" width="640" height="360"></canvas><script>
// One of the cockpit's DAW screens, drawn only from the JTunnel live data the page is
// granted (JStream's page API, `jstream.data()`, ADR-0171 decision 10): ?view= picks
// transport, arrange, device, notes, mixer, clip, scenes, iso, isopads, bridge, bridgepads or panels (or `window.DAW_VIEW`, set by a
// script ahead of this one when the page is given to JStream inline). Everything that moves or
// blinks follows the data (the clock key's beats), never the page's own clock, so a
// render on a held clock draws the same picture every time. `?w=` (or `window.DAW_W`) sets
// the width; the desk's note grid is 600 wide.
const VIEW = window.DAW_VIEW || new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('view') || 'transport';
const cv = document.getElementById('c');
const x = cv.getContext('2d');
const W = +(window.DAW_W || new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('w')) || 640, H = 360, MONO = '"DejaVu Sans Mono",monospace', SANS = 'Inter,"DejaVu Sans",sans-serif';
const AMBER = '255,176,64', CYAN = '110,220,255', GREEN = '70,230,140', RED = '255,70,70';
cv.width = W; document.documentElement.style.width = document.body.style.width = W + 'px';
// The desk's lit pads go on a clear page, over their unlit pads (`isopads`, `bridgepads`).
if (VIEW === 'iso' || VIEW === 'bridge') document.documentElement.style.background = document.body.style.background = 'transparent';
let D = {}, dirty = true;
const lowest = {};   // isomorphic view: the lowest pitch each track has played
const history = [];  // notes view: [beat start, beat end or null, pitch, track]
const steps = {};    // clip view: steps a note started on, per clip
let lastBeats = -1;
const last = {};     // panels view: the last note each track started, [pitch, velocity]
const waves = { master: [], sel: [] }; // panels view: recent levels, newest last
const onsets = {};   // panels view: the beats each track started a note on, the last bar's

function txt(t, px, py, size, col, al = 'left', wt = 600, face = MONO) {
  x.font = `${wt} ${size}px ${face}`; x.textAlign = al; x.fillStyle = col; x.fillText(t, px, py);
}
function rgba(hex, a) {
  const n = parseInt((hex || '#888888').slice(1, 7), 16);
  return `rgba(${n >> 16},${(n >> 8) & 255},${n & 255},${a})`;
}
function frame(title, right) {
  x.fillStyle = '#050709'; x.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);
  const g = x.createRadialGradient(W / 2, H / 2, 0, W / 2, H / 2, W * .6);
  g.addColorStop(0, 'rgba(20,40,60,.35)'); g.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(0,0,0,0)'); x.fillStyle = g; x.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);

  x.fillStyle = `rgba(${AMBER},.8)`; x.fillRect(0, 33, W, 2);
  txt(title, 16, 24, 16, `rgba(${AMBER},.95)`, 'left', 700);

}
function scan() { for (let y = 0; y < H; y += 3) { x.fillStyle = 'rgba(0,0,0,.18)'; x.fillRect(0, y, W, 1); } }
function clock() { return D.clock || { beats: 0, bar: 1, beat: 1, beatPhase: 0, playing: false, tempo: 0 }; }
function blinkOn() { return Math.floor((clock().beats || 0) * 2) % 2 === 0; }
function tracks() {
  const out = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) { const t = D['track/' + i]; if (t && t.exists) out.push(t); }
  return out;
}
function section() {
  const m = (D.markers && D.markers.items) || [], b = clock().beats || 0;
  let cur = null, next = null;
  for (const it of m) { if (it.position <= b) cur = it; else if (!next) next = it; }
  return { cur, next, all: m };
}
function selected() { const g = D.grid || {}; return g.selectedTrack >= 0 ? g.selectedTrack : 0; }
// ---- the desk's pads and meter segments: raised, lit silicone ----
// A pad is a raised silicone cap: matte and dark when unlit, its top edge catching the
// light and its foot casting a short shadow; lit, its light comes up through it, brightest
// in the middle, and spills a little onto the desk around it. A pad lights at once and dims
// over FADE_MS (`?fade=` or `window.DAW_FADE_MS`, default 350) when it turns off. The fade
// is timed by the data's clock while the transport plays, so a render on a held clock draws
// the same picture every time, and by the page's own clock while it is stopped.
const FADE_MS = +(window.DAW_FADE_MS || new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('fade')) || 350;
const DESK_DARK = '#05080c', ROOT_GLOW = 0.3;
const glow = {};      // desk views: each pad's light, by key, [level 0 to 1, colour]
let deskAt = null, fading = false;  // [beats, page ms] at the last draw; a pad still dimming
function deskDt() {   // seconds since the last draw, at most 1
  const c = clock(), ms = performance.now();
  let dt = 0;
  if (deskAt) dt = c.playing && c.tempo > 0 ? ((c.beats || 0) - deskAt[0]) * 60 / c.tempo : (ms - deskAt[1]) / 1000;
  deskAt = [c.beats || 0, ms];

}
// Brings each pad's light to `want` (key -> [level, colour]): up at once, down over
// FADE_MS. Returns whether a pad is still dimming.
function fadeTo(wanted, dt) {
  const want = new Map([...wanted].map(([key, v]) => [String(key), v]));  // keys as `glow`'s
  const k = Math.exp(-dt * 3000 / FADE_MS);

  for (const [key, [lv, col]] of want) { const g = glow[key]; if (!g || lv >= g[0]) glow[key] = [lv, col]; else g[1] = col; }
  for (const key of Object.keys(glow)) {
    const g = glow[key], to = want.has(key) ? want.get(key)[0] : 0;
    if (g[0] > to) { g[0] = to + (g[0] - to) * k; if (g[0] - to < 0.01) g[0] = to; else still = true; }

function rr(px, py, w, h, r) { x.beginPath(); x.roundRect(px, py, w, h, r); }
// An unlit pad; `s` scales its edge and shadow for small pads.
function siliconePad(px, py, w, h, r, s = 1) {
  x.fillStyle = 'rgba(0,0,0,.6)'; rr(px, py + 2.5 * s, w, h, r); x.fill();
  const g = x.createLinearGradient(0, py, 0, py + h);
  g.addColorStop(0, '#2a323d'); g.addColorStop(Math.min(.5, 5 * s / h), '#1d242d'); g.addColorStop(1, '#12171e');
  x.fillStyle = g; rr(px, py, w, h, r); x.fill();

}
// A lit pad, `lv` 0 to 1, in `col`: opaque from ROOT_GLOW up, so it hides the unlit pad
// under it, and fading out below that.
function litPad(px, py, w, h, r, col, lv, s = 1) {
  x.save();
  x.globalAlpha = Math.min(1, lv / ROOT_GLOW);
  x.shadowColor = rgba(col, Math.min(1, .9 * lv)); x.shadowBlur = 16 * s * lv;
  x.fillStyle = '#0c1016'; rr(px, py, w, h, r); x.fill();
  x.shadowBlur = 0;
  x.fillStyle = rgba(col, Math.min(1, lv)); rr(px, py, w, h, r); x.fill();
  const cx = px + w / 2, cy = py + h * .45, g = x.createRadialGradient(cx, cy, 0, cx, cy, Math.max(w, h) * .62);
  g.addColorStop(0, `rgba(255,255,255,${.34 * s * s * lv})`); g.addColorStop(.55, `rgba(255,255,255,${.08 * s * s * lv})`); g.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(0,0,0,.22)');
  x.fillStyle = g; rr(px, py, w, h, r); x.fill();
  x.strokeStyle = `rgba(255,255,255,${.12 + .25 * lv})`; x.lineWidth = 1; rr(px + .5, py + .5, w - 1, h - 1, r); x.stroke();
  x.restore();
}

  const p = h => parseInt(h.slice(1, 7), 16), A = p(a), B = p(b), m = sh => Math.round(((A >> sh) & 255) * (1 - t) + ((B >> sh) & 255) * t);

}
// Calls `f(px, py, w, h, row, column)` for each of the desk's 8 x 8 pads, row 0 at the foot.
function isoPads(f) {
  const cols = 8, rows = 8, gap = 6, cw = (W - gap * (cols + 1)) / cols, ch = (H - gap * (rows + 1)) / rows;
  for (let r = 0; r < rows; r++) for (let c = 0; c < cols; c++) f(gap + c * (cw + gap), H - (r + 1) * (ch + gap), cw, ch, r, c);
}
// Calls `f(key, px, py, w, h, column, segment, segments, height 0 to 1)` for each of the
// meter bridge's segments: six tracks of two bars in the first 290 px, the master's two
// in the last 56, 18 segments each, segment 0 at the foot.
const BRIDGE = [];
for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) for (let sub = 0; sub < 2; sub++) BRIDGE.push({ i, sub, low: '#2fe08a', high: '#ff4a3a', x0: 8 + i * (281 / 6) + sub * ((281 / 6 - 8) / 2 + 2), w: (281 / 6 - 8) / 2 - 2 });
for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) BRIDGE.push({ master: true, i, low: '#6ee0ff', high: '#ffb040', x0: 298 + i * 25, w: 19 });
function bridgeSegs(f) {
  const n = 18, gap = 4, y0 = 8, sh = (H - 2 * y0 - gap * (n - 1)) / n;
  BRIDGE.forEach((col, ci) => {
    for (let s = 0; s < n; s++) f(ci * n + s, col.x0, H - y0 - (s + 1) * sh - s * gap, col.w, sh, col, s, n, (s + .5) / n);
  });
}
function bar(px, py, w, h, v, col) {
  x.fillStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,.06)'; x.fillRect(px, py, w, h);
  x.fillStyle = col; x.fillRect(px, py, w * Math.max(0, Math.min(1, v)), h);
}

// ---- the console panels (the `panels` view) ----
// Each panel's cell in the picture, [x, y, w, h]: keep in step with tools/live_panels.py.
const PANEL_AT = {
  launcher: [0, 0, 160, 160], status: [160, 0, 160, 80], note: [160, 80, 160, 80],
  density: [0, 160, 160, 80], levels: [160, 160, 160, 80], masterWave: [0, 240, 160, 80],
  trackWave: [160, 240, 160, 80], activity: [0, 320, 80, 40], position: [80, 320, 80, 40],
  beats: [160, 320, 80, 40], strips: [240, 320, 80, 40],
};
const AMB = 'rgb(255,150,30)', AMB_DIM = 'rgba(255,150,30,.22)';
const SEG = { 0: 'abcdef', 1: 'bc', 2: 'abged', 3: 'abgcd', 4: 'fgbc', 5: 'afgcd', 6: 'afgedc', 7: 'abc',
  8: 'abcdefg', 9: 'abcdfg', '-': 'g', ' ': '', A: 'abcefg', b: 'fgcde', C: 'adef', d: 'bcdeg',
  E: 'adefg', F: 'aefg', G: 'acdef' };
function seg(ch, px, py, w, h, col) {

  notes() {

  // The desk's pads as an isomorphic note grid, as a grid instrument lays it out: a

  // player (the foot of the picture). The selected track's playing notes light every pad

A browser source's page can be granted the clock, scene names, shared values, audio levels, tempo, MIDI and DAW data, each by its own switch.

<body><canvas id="c" width="640" height="360"></canvas><script>
// One of the cockpit's DAW screens, drawn only from the JTunnel live data the page is
// granted (JStream's page API, `jstream.data()`, ADR-0171 decision 10): ?view= picks
// transport, arrange, device, notes, mixer, clip, scenes, iso, isopads, bridge, bridgepads or panels (or `window.DAW_VIEW`, set by a

<!doctype html><html><head><script>window.DAW_VIEW="clip";window.DAW_W=640</script><meta charset="utf-8"><title>DAW screen</title>

<body><canvas id="c" width="640" height="360"></canvas><script>
// One of the cockpit's DAW screens, drawn only from the JTunnel live data the page is
// granted (JStream's page API, `jstream.data()`, ADR-0171 decision 10): ?view= picks
// transport, arrange, device, notes, mixer, clip, scenes, iso, isopads, bridge, bridgepads or panels (or `window.DAW_VIEW`, set by a
// script ahead of this one when the page is given to JStream inline). Everything that moves or
// blinks follows the data (the clock key's beats), never the page's own clock, so a

let D = {}, dirty = true;
const lowest = {};   // isomorphic view: the lowest pitch each track has played
const history = [];  // notes view: [beat start, beat end or null, pitch, track]
const steps = {};    // clip view: steps a note started on, per clip
let lastBeats = -1;
const last = {};     // panels view: the last note each track started, [pitch, velocity]
const waves = { master: [], sel: [] }; // panels view: recent levels, newest last
const onsets = {};   // panels view: the beats each track started a note on, the last bar's

}
function rgba(hex, a) {

<!doctype html><html><head><script>window.DAW_VIEW="notes";window.DAW_W=640</script><meta charset="utf-8"><title>DAW screen</title>

<body><canvas id="c" width="640" height="360"></canvas><script>

// transport, arrange, device, notes, mixer, clip, scenes, iso, isopads, bridge, bridgepads or panels (or `window.DAW_VIEW`, set by a
// script ahead of this one when the page is given to JStream inline). Everything that moves or
// blinks follows the data (the clock key's beats), never the page's own clock, so a
// render on a held clock draws the same picture every time. `?w=` (or `window.DAW_W`) sets
// the width; the desk's note grid is 600 wide.
const VIEW = window.DAW_VIEW || new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('view') || 'transport';

let D = {}, dirty = true;
const lowest = {};   // isomorphic view: the lowest pitch each track has played
const history = [];  // notes view: [beat start, beat end or null, pitch, track]
const steps = {};    // clip view: steps a note started on, per clip

const last = {};     // panels view: the last note each track started, [pitch, velocity]

}

<!doctype html><html><head><script>window.DAW_VIEW="scenes";window.DAW_W=640</script><meta charset="utf-8"><title>DAW screen</title>

    const c = clock(), s = section(), tr = tracks();
    frame('ARRANGEMENT', `BAR ${c.bar}`);
    const total = s.all.length ? s.all[s.all.length - 1].position + 12 : 196, L = 92, R = W - 54, w = R - L;
    const X = b => L + w * b / total;
    s.all.forEach((m, i) => {
      const end = i + 1 < s.all.length ? s.all[i + 1].position : total, cur = s.cur === m;
      x.fillStyle = cur ? `rgba(${AMBER},.35)` : 'rgba(127,142,163,.14)';
      x.fillRect(X(m.position) + 1, 46, X(end) - X(m.position) - 2, 26);
      txt(m.name.replace('Chorus', 'Ch').replace('Verse', 'V').replace('Pre-tag', 'Pre').toUpperCase(),
          X(m.position) + 4, 64, 11, cur ? '#fff' : `rgba(${CYAN},.75)`, 'left', 700);
    });
    tr.forEach((t, ti) => {
      const y = 86 + ti * 38;
      txt(t.name.toUpperCase(), 14, y + 21, 11, rgba(t.color, .95), 'left', 700);
      s.all.forEach((m, i) => {
        const sl = t.slots[i]; if (!sl || !sl.hasContent) return;
        const end = i + 1 < s.all.length ? s.all[i + 1].position : total, on = sl.state === 'playing';
        x.fillStyle = rgba(t.color, on ? .85 : .3); x.fillRect(X(m.position) + 1, y + 4, X(end) - X(m.position) - 2, 26);
        if (sl.queued === 'play' && blinkOn()) { x.strokeStyle = rgba(t.color, 1); x.lineWidth = 2; x.strokeRect(X(m.position) + 2, y + 5, X(end) - X(m.position) - 4, 24); }
      });
      // its notes as ticks while it plays
      const ns = (D.notes && D.notes.tracks[ti]) || [];
      if (ns.length) { x.fillStyle = '#fff'; x.fillRect(X(c.beats) - 1, y + 4, 3, 26); }
    });
    x.fillStyle = `rgba(${CYAN},.95)`; x.fillRect(X(c.beats || 0) - 1, 42, 2, 86 + tr.length * 38 - 42);
    const ms = (D.meters && D.meters.master) || [0, 0];
    ms.forEach((v, i) => {
      x.fillStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,.07)'; x.fillRect(R + 14 + i * 16, 46, 12, H - 64);
      const g = x.createLinearGradient(0, H - 18, 0, 46); g.addColorStop(0, `rgba(${GREEN},.95)`); g.addColorStop(.75, `rgba(${AMBER},.95)`); g.addColorStop(1, `rgba(${RED},.95)`);
      x.fillStyle = g; const hh = (H - 64) * v; x.fillRect(R + 14 + i * 16, H - 18 - hh, 12, hh);
    });
  },
  device() {
    const d = D.device || {}, ps = d.params || [];
    frame('DEVICE', (d.page && d.page.name || '').toUpperCase() + ' PAGE');
    x.fillStyle = rgba(d.trackColor, .9); x.fillRect(16, 48, 8, 46);
    txt((d.track || '').toUpperCase(), 34, 66, 14, rgba(d.trackColor, 1), 'left', 700);
    txt(`${d.name || ''}  ·  ${d.preset || ''}`, 34, 90, 20, 'rgba(255,255,255,.95)', 'left', 700, SANS);
    ps.slice(0, 8).forEach((p, i) => {
      const cx = 80 + (i % 4) * 160, cy = 160 + Math.floor(i / 4) * 112, r = 30, a0 = Math.PI * .75, span = Math.PI * 1.5;
      x.lineCap = 'round';
      x.strokeStyle = 'rgba(255,255,255,.1)'; x.lineWidth = 7; x.beginPath(); x.arc(cx, cy, r, a0, a0 + span); x.stroke();
      x.strokeStyle = rgba(d.trackColor, .95); x.beginPath(); x.arc(cx, cy, r, a0, a0 + span * p.value); x.stroke();
      if (Math.abs(p.modulated - p.value) > .005) {
        x.strokeStyle = `rgba(${CYAN},.9)`; x.lineWidth = 3; x.beginPath(); x.arc(cx, cy, r + 8, a0 + span * Math.min(p.value, p.modulated), a0 + span * Math.max(p.value, p.modulated)); x.stroke();
      }
      const a = a0 + span * p.modulated; x.strokeStyle = '#fff'; x.lineWidth = 3;
      x.beginPath(); x.moveTo(cx + Math.cos(a) * 10, cy + Math.sin(a) * 10); x.lineTo(cx + Math.cos(a) * (r - 6), cy + Math.sin(a) * (r - 6)); x.stroke();
      txt(p.name.toUpperCase(), cx, cy + r + 18, 11, `rgba(${CYAN},.85)`, 'center', 700);
      txt(p.text, cx, cy + r + 33, 11, 'rgba(255,255,255,.6)', 'center', 500);
    });
    const ch = (d.chain || []).map(c => c.name).join('  ›  ');
    txt(ch, W - 16, 66, 12, `rgba(${AMBER},.7)`, 'right', 500);
  },
  notes() {
    const c = clock(), b = c.beats || 0, tr = tracks();
    frame('NOTES', '');
    const span = 16, L = 16, R = W - 16, X = v => R - (b - v) / span * (R - L);
    const top = 44, low = 38, high = 82, ph = 236, Y = p => top + ph - (p - low) / (high - low) * ph;
    for (let k = Math.ceil(b - span); k <= b; k++) {
      x.fillStyle = k % 4 === 0 ? `rgba(${AMBER},.22)` : 'rgba(255,255,255,.05)'; x.fillRect(X(k), top, 1, H - top - 10);
    }
    for (const n of history) {
      if (n[1] !== null && n[1] < b - span) continue;
      const t = tr[n[3]] || {}, x0 = X(n[0]), x1 = X(n[1] === null ? b : n[1]);
      if (n[2] < 0) { // drums: a lane each at the foot
        const y = 296 + (-n[2] - 1) * 18; x.fillStyle = rgba(t.color, .9); x.fillRect(x0, y, Math.max(3, x1 - x0), 12);
      } else { x.fillStyle = rgba(t.color, n[1] === null ? 1 : .75); x.fillRect(x0, Y(n[2]) - 3, Math.max(3, x1 - x0), 6); }
    }
    ['KICK', 'SNARE', 'HAT'].forEach((s, i) => txt(s, 20, 306 + i * 18, 10, 'rgba(255,255,255,.45)', 'left', 700));
    x.fillStyle = `rgba(${CYAN},.9)`; x.fillRect(R - 1, top, 2, H - top - 10);
    tr.forEach((t, i) => txt(t.name.toUpperCase(), 100 + i * 84, 24, 10, rgba(t.color, 1), 'left', 700));
  },
  mixer() {
    const tr = tracks(), m = (D.meters && D.meters.tracks) || [];
    frame('MIXER', '');
    const n = tr.length + 1, sw = (W - 32) / n;
    tr.concat([{ name: 'Master', color: '#c0c0c0', master: true }]).forEach((t, i) => {
      const px = 16 + i * sw, v = t.master ? ((D.meters && D.meters.master) || [0, 0]) : (m[i] || [0, 0]);
      x.fillStyle = rgba(t.color, .9); x.fillRect(px + 4, 44, sw - 8, 6);
      txt(t.name.toUpperCase().slice(0, 9), px + sw / 2, 68, 11, rgba(t.color, 1), 'center', 700);
      v.forEach((lv, j) => {
        const bx = px + sw / 2 - 14 + j * 16, top = 82, hh = 220, seg = 22;
        for (let k = 0; k < seg; k++) {
          const lit = (k + .5) / seg <= lv, col = k >= seg - 2 ? RED : k >= seg - 6 ? AMBER : GREEN;
          x.fillStyle = `rgba(${col},${lit ? .95 : .08})`; x.fillRect(bx, top + hh - (k + 1) * hh / seg + 1, 12, hh / seg - 2);
        }
      });
      if (!t.master) {
        const sl = t.slots && t.slots[t.playing];
        txt(t.playing >= 0 ? '▶' : '■', px + sw / 2, 326, 14, t.playing >= 0 ? `rgba(${GREEN},.95)` : 'rgba(255,255,255,.3)', 'center', 700, SANS);
        if (t.selected) { x.strokeStyle = `rgba(${CYAN},.8)`; x.lineWidth = 2; x.strokeRect(px + 2, 38, sw - 4, 300); }
      }
    });
  },
  clip() {
    const cl = D.clip || {}, c = clock(), key = `${cl.track}/${cl.scene}`;
    frame('CLIP', cl.loop ? 'LOOP' : '');
    x.fillStyle = rgba(cl.color, .9); x.fillRect(16, 48, 8, 46);
    txt((cl.name || '').toUpperCase(), 34, 78, 22, 'rgba(255,255,255,.95)', 'left', 700, SANS);
    const bars = Math.max(1, Math.round((cl.loopLength || 16) / 4)), rows = Math.min(8, bars), step = cl.playingStep;
    const L = 34, T = 112, cw = (W - 34 - 24) / 16, rh = Math.min(26, (H - T - 20) / rows);
    const hit = steps[key] || {};
    for (let r = 0; r < rows; r++) for (let s = 0; s < 16; s++) {
      const i = r * 16 + s, past = cl.playing && step >= 0 && i < step, now = cl.playing && i === step;
      x.fillStyle = now ? '#fff' : hit[i] ? rgba(cl.color, past ? .95 : .4) : past ? rgba(cl.color, .18) : 'rgba(255,255,255,.05)';
      x.fillRect(L + s * cw + 2, T + r * rh + 2, cw - 4, rh - 4);
    }
    txt(`${bars} BARS  ·  STEP ${step >= 0 ? step + 1 : '-'}`, W - 24, 78, 13, `rgba(${CYAN},.8)`, 'right', 600);
  },
  // The desk's pads as an isomorphic note grid, as a grid instrument lays it out: a
  // semitone to the right, a fourth (5 semitones) up a row, the lowest row nearest the
  // player (the foot of the picture). The selected track's playing notes light every pad
  // of their pitch in its colour, brighter with velocity (0 to 127); each C glows faintly. The grid
  // starts on the C at or below the lowest note the track has played, and a note out of its
  // range folds onto it by octaves. Only the lit pads are drawn, on a clear page: the unlit
  // pads are `isopads`, a picture of their own under this one, so the scene can dim them
  // with its lights and leave the lit ones glowing. A pad lights at once and dims over
  // FADE_MS when its note ends.
  iso() {
    const g = D.grid || {}, sel = g.selectedTrack >= 0 ? g.selectedTrack : 0;
    const t = D['track/' + sel] || {}, playing = ((D.notes && D.notes.tracks) || [])[sel] || [];
    const lo = lowest[sel] !== undefined ? lowest[sel] : 36, base = Math.min(Math.floor(lo / 12) * 12, 72);
    // A note above or below the grid folds onto it by whole octaves, so any range shows:
    // too high comes up from the foot, too low comes down from the top.
    const top = base + 7 + 5 * 7, vel = new Map();
    for (const [p, v] of playing) {
      let q = p;
      while (q > top) q -= 12;
      while (q < base) q += 12;
      vel.set(q, Math.max(vel.get(q) || 0, v));
    }
    const want = new Map(), roots = new Map();
    isoPads((px, py, cw, ch, r, c) => {
      const pitch = base + c + 5 * r, key = r * 8 + c;
      if (vel.has(pitch)) want.set(key, [0.55 + 0.45 * Math.min(1, (vel.get(pitch) || 127) / 127), t.color]);
      else if (pitch % 12 === 0) want.set(key, [ROOT_GLOW, t.color]);
      if (pitch % 12 === 0) roots.set(key, 'C' + (pitch / 12 - 2));
    });
    fading = fadeTo(want, deskDt());
    x.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);
    isoPads((px, py, cw, ch, r, c) => {
      const key = r * 8 + c, gl = glow[key];
      if (gl) litPad(px, py, cw, ch, 6, gl[1], gl[0]);
      const name = roots.get(key);
      if (name && gl) {
        x.globalAlpha = Math.min(1, gl[0] / ROOT_GLOW);
        txt(name, px + 7, py + ch - 8, 11, gl[0] > ROOT_GLOW + 0.05 ? 'rgba(0,0,0,.55)' : 'rgba(255,255,255,.4)', 'left', 700);
        x.globalAlpha = 1;
      }
    });
  },
  // The desk's unlit pads, under `iso`: the same 8 x 8 pads, every one unlit, on the
  // desk's dark. It needs no data and never changes.
  isopads() {
    x.fillStyle = DESK_DARK; x.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);
    isoPads((px, py, cw, ch) => siliconePad(px, py, cw, ch, 6));
  },
  // The desk's meter bridge, beside the pads: the six tracks (left and right each) and the
  // master, in 18 segments, lit from the foot by `meters`, green to red (the master cyan
  // to amber). Each segment is a small lit pad that dims over FADE_MS as the level falls.
  // Only the lit segments are drawn, on a clear page, over `bridgepads`.
  bridge() {
    const m = D.meters || {}, tr = m.tracks || [], ms = m.master || [], want = new Map();
    bridgeSegs((key, px, py, w, h, col, s, n, at) => {
      const v = col.master ? ms[col.i] : (tr[col.i] || [])[col.sub];
      if (+v >= (s + 1) / n - 0.5 / n) want.set(key, [1, mixHex(col.low, col.high, at)]);
    });
    fading = fadeTo(want, deskDt());
    x.clearRect(0, 0, W, H);
    bridgeSegs((key, px, py, w, h) => { const gl = glow[key]; if (gl) litPad(px, py, w, h, 2, gl[1], gl[0], 0.5); });
  },
  // The meter bridge's unlit segments, under `bridge`.
  bridgepads() {
    x.fillStyle = DESK_DARK; x.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);
    bridgeSegs((key, px, py, w, h) => siliconePad(px, py, w, h, 2, 0.5));
  },
  // The console's small displays, live: one 320 x 360 picture holding every panel, each in
  // the cell the model's live-panel quads map (cockpit-3d/tools/live_panels.py, PANELS).
  panels() {
    x.fillStyle = '#000'; x.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);
    for (const [name, [px, py, w, h]] of Object.entries(PANEL_AT)) {
      x.save(); x.translate(px, py);
      x.fillStyle = 'rgb(10,6,3)'; x.fillRect(2, 2, w - 4, h - 4);
      x.beginPath(); x.rect(2, 2, w - 4, h - 4); x.clip();
      panel[name](w, h); x.restore();
    }
  },
  scenes() {
    const sc = (D.scenes && D.scenes.items) || [], g = D.grid || {}, tr = tracks();
    frame('SCENES', `${g.trackCount || 0} TRACKS`);
    let cur = -1, queued = -1;
    for (const t of tr) for (const sl of t.slots) { if (sl.state === 'playing') cur = sl.scene; if (sl.queued === 'play') queued = sl.scene; }
    sc.forEach((s, i) => {
      const y = 44 + i * 38, on = i === cur, q = i === queued;
      x.fillStyle = on ? `rgba(${GREEN},.22)` : 'rgba(255,255,255,.04)'; x.fillRect(16, y, W - 32, 32);
      x.fillStyle = on ? `rgba(${GREEN},.95)` : q && blinkOn() ? `rgba(${GREEN},.95)` : 'rgba(255,255,255,.2)';
      x.beginPath(); x.moveTo(30, y + 7); x.lineTo(48, y + 16); x.lineTo(30, y + 25); x.fill();
      txt(s.name.toUpperCase(), 62, y + 22, 15, on ? '#fff' : `rgba(${CYAN},.8)`, 'left', 700);
      txt(`${s.clips} CLIPS`, W - 28, y + 22, 12, 'rgba(255,255,255,.45)', 'right', 500);
      tr.forEach((t, ti) => {
        const sl = t.slots[i]; if (!sl || !sl.hasContent) return;
        x.fillStyle = rgba(t.color, sl.state === 'playing' ? 1 : .35); x.fillRect(300 + ti * 34, y + 9, 26, 14);

    });
  },
};

function take() {
  D = jstream.data();
  const c = clock(), b = c.beats || 0;
  if (b < lastBeats - 1) { history.length = 0; for (const k in onsets) delete onsets[k]; }
  lastBeats = b;
  // keep a short history of the notes for the piano roll and the clip's steps
  const ns = (D.notes && D.notes.tracks) || [];
  const open = new Map();
  history.forEach((n, i) => { if (n[1] === null) open.set(`${n[3]}:${n[2]}`, i); });
  const seen = new Set();
  ns.forEach((list, ti) => list.forEach(([p, v]) => {
    if (lowest[ti] === undefined || p < lowest[ti]) lowest[ti] = p;
    const pitch = ti === 0 ? -({ 36: 1, 38: 2, 42: 3 }[p] || 3) : p, k = `${ti}:${pitch}`;
    seen.add(k);
    if (!open.has(k)) {
      last[ti] = [p, v];
      (onsets[ti] = onsets[ti] || []).push(b);
      history.push([b, null, pitch, ti]);
      const cl = D.clip || {}, t = D['track/' + ti];
      if (cl.playing && t && t.name === cl.track && cl.playingStep >= 0) {
        const key = `${cl.track}/${cl.scene}`; (steps[key] = steps[key] || {})[cl.playingStep] = 1;
      }

  open.forEach((i, k) => { if (!seen.has(k)) history[i][1] = b; });
  while (history.length > 1500) history.shift();
  const lvl = m => m ? Math.max(m[0] || 0, m[1] || 0) : 0, mt = (D.meters && D.meters.tracks) || [];
  waves.master.push(lvl(D.meters && D.meters.master)); waves.sel.push(lvl(mt[selected()]));
  for (const k in waves) while (waves[k].length > 120) waves[k].shift();
  for (const k in onsets) onsets[k] = onsets[k].filter(t => t > b - 4);
  dirty = true;
}
function draw() {
  if (VIEW === 'isopads' || VIEW === 'bridgepads') { if (dirty) { views[VIEW](); dirty = false; } }
  else if (window.jstream && jstream.data) { if (dirty || fading) { views[VIEW](); if (!['iso', 'bridge', 'panels'].includes(VIEW)) scan(); dirty = false; } }
  else { frame('DAW', 'NO PAGE API'); scan(); }
  requestAnimationFrame(draw);
}
if (window.jstream && jstream.addEventListener) jstream.addEventListener('data', take);
requestAnimationFrame(draw);
</script></body></html>

bookmarks.name: Welcome
bookmarks.note:
This is JStream. It's a live streaming and compositing studio, written from scratch in Rust. It does the job of a studio like OBS: scenes, sources, mixing, streaming and recording.

It's pre-release, and the show features you're about to see arrive in the next pre-release.

And everything you're watching right now is a JStream project, run by a JStream show. None of it is a video.

bookmarks.name: The studio
bookmarks.note:
Here's the studio. A scene is a stack of sources: cameras, screen and window capture, media, browser pages, text, timers and audio visualisers. They're composited on the GPU, and every item can be cropped, turned in 3D, blended and given effects, live.

Edits undo per client. My undo never takes back a change somebody else made, from a browser, the command line or an agent.

And outputs take video mixes and audio buses, not scenes, so the stream and the recording can carry different pictures and sound.

bookmarks.name: What you make
bookmarks.note:
Here's the kind of scene you can make. This is a live JStream scene, not a picture of one.

Every piece is a built-in source: the feeds are images, cropped to 16:9 in the scene, the clock is a timer, and the lower third is a scene of its own, shown here as one layer.

*The footage is from Tears of Steel, the Blender Foundation's open film, under CC BY.*

bookmarks.name: Keyframes
bookmarks.note:
Now the part I'm most excited about: keyframes.

This is one scene, called Mission feed. A keyframe is a saved arrangement of that same scene. It can change where each item sits, its size, crop, opacity, whether it shows, and its effects.

Watch: Two-up. Close-up. Main feed. Every item glides at once, and each item can have its own delay. See the small picture land a beat late?

The show is loading these keyframes right now. A sequence, a hotkey or a MIDI pad can load them too.

bookmarks.name: Motion
bookmarks.note:
Items can also move on their own, with no keyframes at all. These are motion modifiers.

Wiggle is seeded noise. Oscillate follows a waveform. Drift is a steady rate. Impulse fires on a cue, and the show is kicking it right now. Audio follows a sound level.

MIDI, live data and channels can drive them too. They work on position, scale, rotation, opacity and effect settings, and on scene cameras.

bookmarks.name: Sequences & channels
bookmarks.note:
Sequences move values over time.

A channel is one number. MIDI, live data, keys, cues or a lane on a sequence can move it, and positions, cameras, effects and live settings can follow it.

A sequence has lanes, which are curves on channels, and cues, which are actions on a clock. It can even start itself: when a channel rises, a keyframe loads, a scene shows, or you press a key.

bookmarks.name: Shows
bookmarks.note:
And this is what's running the whole presentation: a show.

One timeline, with program, overlay, keyframe, sequence and audio tracks, saved with the project. Bookmarks pause or play through. Loops hold, like a waiting room, until I press Continue.

I can jump to any bookmark, and the studio is set the way playing there would have left it.

And the notes I'm reading right now? They're this bookmark's note.

bookmarks.name: 3D cockpit
bookmarks.note:
Scenes can be 3D. It's opt in, per scene: give a scene a camera and its items get depth. Most scenes stay 2D.

Here's one example, a glTF cockpit rendered in JStream. Any 2D scene, like a camera feed, can play on the model's monitor.

The screens show Bitwig, live, over JTunnel. Here the session is simulated. Bitwig sends the clock and tempo, transport, clip grid and scenes, track meters, notes, mixer, device, clip and markers. Pages draw it, and data modifiers map any of it onto the scene. Here the meters drive the cabin lights.

bookmarks.name: DAW & web pages
bookmarks.note:
JStream connects to your music setup.

JTunnel is a CLAP plugin. It sends a track's audio and MIDI over the local network, and JStream takes the audio as a source and the MIDI as bindings. You accept each sender first.

In Bitwig, JTunnel also sends the clip grid, transport and device. And a browser source's page can read JStream's clock, scenes, levels, tempo, MIDI and DAW data, each behind its own switch.

bookmarks.name: Keys & MIDI
bookmarks.note:
Control works one way for everything. Hotkeys, MIDI controllers and tempo sync share one binding system.

A key or a pad runs the same actions the buttons do: switch scenes, load keyframes, play sequences, go live.

*This bookmark continues by itself after 12 seconds.*

bookmarks.name: Effects
bookmarks.note: Effects, quickly. Built-in filters work on sources, items, scenes and outputs. And for anything beyond those, you can write shader sources and filters as WGSL effect packs.

bookmarks.name: Plugins
bookmarks.note: Automation plugins run sandboxed. A plugin only gets the access its manifest asks for and you grant. And if an update asks for more, it stays off until you grant it again.

bookmarks.name: Cameras & going live
bookmarks.note:
PTZ cameras: drive them from the panel, recall shots from a key, and map pan, tilt, zoom and focus to MIDI. A scene can carry each camera's shot, so switching the scene aims the cameras.

Going live: RTMP or RTMPS to YouTube or any service with a stream key, a recording at the same time, and a virtual camera on Windows and Linux. Each stream or recording gets its own encoder, mix and bus.

*The stats panel is from a test engine, so its numbers are illustrative.*

bookmarks.name: Under the hood
bookmarks.note:
Under the hood.

Everything is an API. The app is just one client of the protocol, so a script, the command line, or an AI agent over MCP can drive almost anything a person can.

It's Rust, and the real-time audio thread never allocates, locks or blocks. Tests enforce that. It runs headless too. And it's open source, MIT or Apache-2.0.

bookmarks.name: Thanks
bookmarks.note:
Thank you! Happy to take questions.

*The Outro loop finishes its pass when you press Continue. Then the show goes back to the Pre-show, ready to run again.*

bookmarks.name: Pre-show
bookmarks.note:
*Be right back slate, looping until you press Continue. The transport on it is live.*

In a moment I'll take you into the cockpit.

*Make sure Bitwig is playing, or the simulated session is, then press Continue.*

bookmarks.name: Power up
bookmarks.note:
This is a starship cockpit, and it's a real 3D model: a glTF file that JStream lights and renders live, with reflections, bloom and depth of field.

Watch it power up. The lights come up in stages, and then the monitors flicker on one by one. Each of those is a sequence: a short timeline that moves a few channels.

Everything on those screens is coming from Bitwig, live, over JTunnel.

bookmarks.name: The pilot's seat
bookmarks.note:
Let's sit down. The camera views are sequences too: each one glides the scene camera from wherever it is to the view, so I can cut between them on a key, a MIDI note or a cue in this show.

From the pilot's seat you see the three monitors wrapped around you, and the desk below them.

bookmarks.name: The desk
bookmarks.note:
The desk is the musician's view. The pad grid is an isomorphic note layout for the track selected in Bitwig: the notes it's playing light up in that track's colour.

The bars beside it are the meter bridge, every track and the master. And the lights over the desk swell with each track's level, in its colour.

bookmarks.name: The monitors
bookmarks.note:
The centre monitor is the arrangement, with the play head and the song's sections.

On the left, the transport: tempo, bar and beat, and the section we're in. On the right, the device on the selected track and its parameters.

These are web pages drawn from JStream's page API. JStream hands them Bitwig's state, and they draw it.

bookmarks.name: Overhead and the consoles
bookmarks.note:
Overhead, the mixer and Bitwig's scenes. On the left console, the clip that's playing; on the right, the notes it's sending.

Even the small readouts on the consoles are live: the last note and its velocity, how busy the track is, and the level traces.

bookmarks.name: Warp
bookmarks.note:
Out the windshield is the sky: an environment light with stars and nebulae.

The warp is a channel. A sequence takes it up to full, and a CC or a JTunnel Mod from Bitwig can drive the same channel, so a knob in the DAW can fly the ship.

And when we drop out, we arrive somewhere new.

bookmarks.name: Hologram
bookmarks.note:
Incoming transmission. The hologram projects up out of the dash: a lens flare, a beam, and a panel showing any source, a camera or a screen capture.

It's a filter on a regular source, placed in the 3D scene.

bookmarks.name: The same data in 2D
bookmarks.note:
And not every scene has to be 3D. This is the same live Bitwig data as a flat desk: the clip launcher, the meters, the transport, the mixer and the arrangement.

The studio keeps the cockpit warm, so switching back is instant.

bookmarks.name: Power down
bookmarks.note:
And that's the cockpit. Monitors off, lights off.

Thanks for flying with us.

*Continue goes back to the pre-show slate.*
